propositions: Core push delivery performs five compare-and-set retry cycles followed by exactly one conditional terminal push, entered only after a retriable rejection produces a clean merged HEAD; earlier success exits without terminal push.

Strict delivery mode raises catchable PushDeliveryError with stable reason vocabulary and git detail, while best-effort mode (default) returns None and preserves legacy caller behavior for all pre-existing library, CLI, MCP, and store-write operations.
The private Python module adapter translates PushDeliveryError to stderr and nonzero exit at the process boundary without calling sys.exit from core or emitting ticket events or BRIDGE_ALERT.

All existing callers across event append, batch append, NDJSON import, transition close, delete, compact, and claim operations omit strict parameter or reach core with strict=False, inheriting only the corrected retry budget while retaining legacy disposition.

Distinct stable reasons classify policy declines (GH013 branch protection markers) separately from transport failures (timeouts, network, other), preserving operational continuity and the distinction surfaced in prior investigations.

Dirty-tree staging and committing remain outside push_tickets_branch and are owned by dependent operations; push_tickets_branch owns only destination resolution, push/fetch/merge recovery, and no add/commit/event work.
